Name: batch_size_grokking
Title: Batch Size Grokking: Assessing the impact of the training batchsize on the grokking phenomenon
Experiment: Modify the experiments to dynamically adjust the batch size during training, starting with a small batch size and gradually increasing it. This could potentially lead to faster generalization on the validation set.

Name: capacity_grokking
Title: Sizing Up Grokking: How Model Capacity Governs the Memorisation–Generalisation Transition
Experiment: Expose --num_layers and --dim_model flags. Set num_heads = max(1, dim_model // 32) for divisibility. Grid: num_layers ∈ {1,2,4}, dim_model ∈ {64,128,256}. For each run record: parameter_count, step_when_train_acc_95, step_when_val_acc_95, step_val_acc_99. Compute grokking_gap = val95_step - train95_step. Plot grokking_gap and step_val_acc_99 versus log(parameter_count) across all four datasets. Analyse whether capacity lengthens or shortens the gap and affects sample efficiency.

Name: weight_decay_phase
Title: The Regularisation Phase Transition: Mapping Grokking as a Function of Weight Decay
Experiment: Expose a --weight_decay flag in experiment.py (passed to AdamW). Grid-search wd ∈ {0.0,1e-4,3e-4,1e-3,3e-3,1e-2,3e-2,1e-1,3e-1}. For each dataset and three seeds, log: step_train_acc_95, step_val_acc_95, step_val_acc_99, final accuracies. Define grok_gap = step_val95 - step_train95 (−1 if val never ≥.95). Implement optional early-stop: if both train and val acc stay <0.2 for 3000 updates, terminate run. Aggregate results, plot grok_gap and step_val_acc_99 vs log10(wd) for every task to reveal a critical weight-decay band that maximises the grokking gap, supporting a phase-transition view of implicit regularisation.
